title: A huge amount of money
paragraphs: So, without further ado, we’ll head straight into Faubrey Castle to request an audience. It should be about time he’s awake by now. We timed our arrival just right. If we’d gone in the afternoon, King Faubrey would undoubtedly still have been asleep, and we’d have been kept waiting. King Faubrey, who had summoned us, seemed slightly surprised by our arrival, but he handled it fairly quickly, and we were granted an audience with him.
“Hahaha… Well met, Shield Hero and Spear Hero. I am King Faubrey!”
Just like before, a raucous fanfare rings out. Oh, so he’s still alive. He still looks like a monster, as always. But he’s surprisingly competent.

I scan the room, looking for the minister who usually steps in to defend Takt. …He’s not here. Well, since the Takt commotion is already starting to die down, I suppose he’s already been dealt with? Father nudges me in the side and asks,
“What’s that? A human? A Therianthrope? It’s a race I’ve never seen before, I suppose…”
He seems at a loss for words as he asks me anxiously. So I answer just as I did back then.
“I don’t know. But I’ve heard that those chosen as heroes generation after generation are either married into the royal family or otherwise incorporated into the bloodline.”

“So the royal family of Faubrey is essentially a lineage that condenses the bloodlines of the Four Holy Heroes and the Seven Star Heroes from generation to generation? It just looks to me like a big mix—all sorts of things reacting with each other.”

Hahaha, that’s Father for you. I think that’s pretty much the gist of it. You could say they’re the ultimate hybrid—a natural chimera—born from the excessive mixing of humans, Demi-Humans, and Therianthropes.

As we’re talking about this, King Faubrey is acting just as he always does, licking his lips as he looks at Yuki-chan and the others. Yuki-chan, Sakura-chan, and Kou are all licking their lips in a similar way, just like before. If you eat something like that, you’ll get an upset stomach, you know?
“W-what’s with these guys? They’re acting weird.”
“If you reversed your panda transformation, wouldn’t you be able to fit right in with the group?”
“No way, what’s the point of doing something so pointless?”
By the way, Father has already seen the panda in its pig-form. I’m not interested, so I didn’t look, though.
“Even if that lecherous, cruel king takes a liking to us… well, let’s just say I’d rather he didn’t.”
After exchanging a few quiet remarks like that, we’ll introduce ourselves. I’ll go first!
“My name is Motoyasu Kitamura! I’m The Love Hunter!”
“And… the Spear Hero, who made a tremendous contribution to ending the foolish war started by Shieldfreeden.”
The representative of the Shusaku race explained something after I spoke. When I looked in that direction, for some reason, Father was giving a thumbs-up.
“I’m Werner, one of the four representatives of the Siltvelt… though I’ve already introduced myself, haven’t I? Well then, Shield Hero—”
“My name is Naofumi Iwatani, summoned as the Shield Hero. Also with me are Sakura-chan, Yuki-chan, Kou, and Rasasusa-san.”
I’m introducing the members who are currently active as my companions. Seeing this, the Pig King seems to be in a good mood for some reason.

“Buhahaha… Well done on fending off countless conspiracies and battles to arrive here in Faubrey in such fine style. The Shield Hero and Spear Hero. Um… well, I’m sure you’re aware, but this time it concerns the war sparked by the conspiracies and grudges of Takt, Alsaholn, and Faubrey.”
“Yes.”

Father is nodding, but his gaze is fixed on the cheat sheet prepared by the Pig King’s subordinates. He’s looking at it with a skeptical expression, as if to ask if this is really going to be okay. So, I nod at Father to reassure him that it’ll be fine.
“First, we must confirm the perspective of the Shield Heroes and Spear Heroes. Would you mind explaining this incident from the very beginning?”
“O-okay. Um…”
Father seems to be organizing his thoughts on where to start before explaining.
“After being summoned to Melromarc and going through all sorts of things, we arrived in Siltvelt. There, we were granted an audience with the Claw Hero, one of the Seven Star Heroes of Siltvelt.”
“It’s only natural for the Seven Star Heroes to greet the Shield Hero and Spear Hero now that they’ve finally arrived.”
“Yes. That’s when Motoyasu, the Spear Hero, saw through the Claw Hero’s disguise. Then, the monster posing as the Claw Hero revealed its true form.”
That was actually Beastrans reacting on its own… but if I explain in detail, I might give away too much, so I’m just giving the gist of it. That creature is undoubtedly the fox under Takt’s command.

“After defeating the monster, we were intensifying our search for the real Hero of the Claw when Takt arrived, claiming it was for diplomatic purposes, intending to coordinate our efforts to take on the Wave. Looking back now, it was likely so he could confirm that the monster—his own hand-picked subordinate—had been killed.”
“Hmm…”

“And so, after confirming the monster’s corpse, Takt tried to ambush us and trap us right before the wave struck. Fortunately, we turned the tables on him and defeated Takt, but in the process, all of his subordinates fled, and they started a war in revenge—that is the full story behind this upheaval.”
“I see… Indeed, the Shield Hero’s account does align with the testimony from the Siltvelt side. It seems there’s no doubt that the root cause of this incident lies entirely with Takt’s side.”

At that moment, Father confided in me that he had secretly wondered, “Is this king really thinking before he answers?” Apparently, it’s because he had simply regurgitated what Father had said. Indeed, mere consistency with what Siltvelt said isn’t proof in and of itself.
This is—well, you know. It’s the kind of situation where the answer has already been decided in advance.
“We’ve already taken various steps regarding this matter. We’re currently tracking down members of factions under Takt’s influence and freezing their powers. They’ve been acting far too recklessly.”

The members of the Takt faction have only one goal. It’s revenge against us for taking down Takt, the man who let them do whatever they pleased. They’re a truly foolish lot. I’ll wipe out every last one of them who wastes their time on such futile endeavors.
“Fortunately, it seems there are some leaking information. They’ve determined they can identify most of them.”

This is just like that, isn’t it? There are pigs of the same kind as the Crimson Swine, who flip-flop the moment the Wind changes. Pigs are pigs after all, but I can tell the difference in their behavior. There are even some useful ones among them, like Lazy Pigs and Stalker Pigs.
“So, what happened to the guy who was the representative of Shieldfreeden?”
When I asked, King Faubrey furrowed his brow. I’m pretty sure there was a guy like that. He was in cahoots with Takt and was manipulating Shieldfreeden, wasn’t he?

“The story goes that after losing the war, once it came to light that he’d started it by lying and deceiving people, he fled somewhere with a vast fortune and items of great magical value. We’re still tracking him down.”
“A vast fortune… Do you think he’ll be all right?”
“That’s a concern of mine as well. Um… I hear it’s on par with the national budget.”
“It’s hopeless—they’ll slip up and run as soon as they’re exposed.”
“That’s certainly true. That said, shouldn’t the handling of Shieldfreeden, with that man at its head, already have been entrusted to Siltvelt?”
“Yes, it has been decided that our nation, Siltvelt, will issue a call for surrender to them, and they have agreed to accept it.”
The Shusaku clan agreed with King Faubrey’s statement. Well, that’s the end of Shieldfreeden, then.

“However… the problem lies with the factions on the run—including the former representative of Shieldfreeden—and those who have secretly allied themselves with Takt. I’ve determined that we have no choice but to continue rooting them out.”
“I suppose so.”
They really are a hopeless bunch. This is entirely my fault. It’s a real blow that we didn’t wipe out the Takt faction back then…

“The loss of the Bow Hero’s life due to this pointless conflict is also extremely grave. Therefore, both the Kingdom of Faubrey and the Kingdom of Siltvelt have decided to place a bounty on the remaining members of the Takt faction.”

Oh? So this is what’s commonly known as a nationwide wanted notice, isn’t it? All things considered, isn’t it rare in this world for someone to be wanted on this scale? Even during the incident where Father’s Finacée was kidnapped, the search only extended as far as the vicinity of Melromarc.

As for the Crimson Swine… I believe a bounty was placed on him on a global scale, wasn’t it? But in that case, it was just the queen personally offering the reward, so the scale is completely different from a major crime with a formal warrant issued by Faubrey.

“Those who harbor individuals believed to belong to the faction will face severe punishment, while those who provide decisive information or capture the remnants will be awarded a substantial bounty.”

It seems that the moment it comes to light that someone is harboring a fugitive, it becomes a crime severe enough to warrant harsh punishment for the entire family. With this, the members of the Takt faction won’t be able to step into the public eye. The only time they’ll come out is when they face Judgment.
“We extend our gratitude to King Faubrey, Siltvelt, the Shield Hero, and the Spear Hero…”
“Very well. We, too, have ended up saddled with a rather troublesome self-proclaimed hero. All we can do is hope for the swift capture of the remnants… Bwahahahaha.”

This explains it, doesn’t it? It’s exactly why he’s the Pig King—he’s licking his lips, eager to devour his prey. And so, at the Pig King’s orders, the Takt faction became wanted not just in Faubrey, but all over the world.

“As for the rest… well. I’m assigning the two of the Four Holy Heroes the task of quelling the waves across the world. I want you to continue your activities. Faubrey will also assist the heroes in their efforts.”
“Ah, yes.”

This is an issue we simply must address. That said, as long as I’m here, along with Father and Lord Filolial and the others, it shouldn’t be a problem we can’t handle. And so, we were asked to deal with the remnants of the Takt faction and to participate in the Waves.
“Is there anything else? Buhahaha.”
“Well…”
Father looked at me, nodded, and then turned his gaze to the Pig King.
“Um… Motoyasu, the Spear Hero, can see events that might occur in the future through his special spear.”

Since it’s hard to get people to easily believe that we’ve been looping time over and over, Father said later that this was just a starting point. In fact, based on my looping experiences so far, I can do things that resemble precognition.
“I see… Does the Spear Hero possess such a power?”
“Yes. That power was also involved when I saw through the monster that Takt had been raising.”
“Hmm…”
Now’s my chance. I’ll step forward a bit here.
“The future is like looking at countless branching worlds. For example, there was a world where, based on a single choice in how we proceeded, Faubrey ended up under Takt’s control.”
“Something like that?”

“I think you have plenty of clues, don’t you? If Takt—with all those crimes to his name—had continued to expand his influence without ever showing his true colors, what do you think would have happened?”
“The possibility isn’t zero, but it’s a bit too late to be talking about it now. Buhahaha.”
“I won’t deny that.”
It’s very difficult to get people to believe in the future. It’s just like how you can’t win Ren and Itsuki over without making use of various factors.
“But… thanks to that power, I was helped when I escaped from Melromarc.”
This is where Father steps in to give me a push. Just as I’d expect from him. In this world, I was desperate to save Father. After all, out of all the worlds, I barely made it in time here.
“Our subordinates have also testified that the Spear Hero possesses such power. Siltvelt has determined that dismissing this as a lie would be foolish.”
“Hahaha… Well, it would be nice if you could tell me something about the future.”

Hmm… Was there any information about a promising future involving the Pig King? The only future that comes to mind is one where I might be disposed of by Takt. The best I can do is feed him to the pigs.
“…Apparently, there are countless beings like Takt in this world.”
Just as I was struggling to come up with a reply, Father explained it like that.
“There are a second and third Takt in this world?”

“Yes. The story goes that assassins dispatched to this world by the mastermind behind the Waves are lying in wait… It’s said those individuals possess the power to steal Seven Star Weapons and the like…”
“Certainly, if that’s true, they could pose a significant threat, but…”
“Your Majesty? They have characteristics similar to Takt’s, you know? You understand, right?”
Father, having sensed the Pig King’s preferences, spoke in a suggestive tone.

“Why not just summon the Seven-Star Heroes on a global scale? If they can conclusively prove they’re the rightful owners, that would serve as proof for us too, and we could narrow things down quite a bit based on the Second Takt, right?”
The Pig King’s eyes lit up at Father’s reply. He’s convinced he’s going to get his hands on a pig.

“Buhahaha. Sounds good. Then let’s summon all the already-selected Seven-Star Heroes to Faubrey. Anyone who ignores the summons will be deemed an evil threat to world peace, and a hefty bounty will be placed on their heads. We’ll root out every Seven-Star Hero on a global scale.”
“Assuming nothing in particular has happened during this period… isn’t there someone lurking around here who possesses a Seven-Star Weapon of the Throwing Type?”
I said this while pulling out a map. Based on my experience with the loops so far, that’s a distinct possibility.
“The adventurer who’s been rising to prominence in that area is ‘Black.’”
Since his official name is unclear, let’s just answer that way. I’m pretty sure his name was something like “Cola” or something like that… but I’ve forgotten.
“Then let’s have it verified.”
As the Pig King raises his hand, Faubrey’s covert unit comes into view.
“Go and gather evidence.”
“‘Yes, sir!’”
With that, they vanished.
“I hope the prophecy of the Spear Hero proves true. Well then, I’ll take my leave… Bwahahaha.”
And just like that, the audience with the Pig King came to an end. It seems the conversation went smoothly, but Father looks exhausted.
